title: Bear scat
def: Black bear scat is a large tubular or piled dropping, often full of berries, seeds, nut shells, grass, or hair, that means a bear has been in the area.
look: thick tubes about 1.5 to 2 inches (4 to 5 cm) wide, or loose piles
packed with berries, seeds, or grass in summer and fall
use: Fresh, moist scat means a bear was there recently. Make noise, keep food sealed and away from camp, and consider moving on.
not: Do not touch or sniff scat with bare hands; use a stick, and wash your hands after. Do not camp next to a latrine or fresh bear sign.
alike: Coyote scat: thinner, twisted, full of hair and bone with tapered ends
Moose summer scat: loose cow-pie clumps of plant fiber

title: Coyote or fox scat
def: Coyote and fox scat is a twisted, rope-like dropping full of hair and small bones, with a tapered end, often left in the middle of a trail.
look: coyote scat about 3/4 to 1 inch (2 to 2.5 cm) wide; fox scat thinner
packed with fur, bone, berries, or seeds
use: Scat on a trail or at a junction is a territory marker. It tells you which predators use the area.
not: Do not touch or sniff scat with bare hands; use a stick, and wash your hands after. Do not camp next to a latrine or fresh bear sign. Canine scat can carry tapeworm eggs.
alike: Domestic dog: usually smooth, uniform, kibble-based, without hair
Bobcat scat: segmented, blunt ends, often partly buried
ask: Tell me about coyote or fox scat

title: Moose scat
def: Moose scat is a pile of large oval pellets of compressed wood fiber in winter, or soft clumps like a cow pie in summer.
look: pellets about 1 to 1 1/2 inches (2.5 to 4 cm) long, much bigger than deer
sawdust-like texture when broken
use: Fresh piles mean moose are using the area; give any moose plenty of room.
not: Do not touch or sniff scat with bare hands; use a stick, and wash your hands after. Do not camp next to a latrine or fresh bear sign.
alike: Deer scat: same shape, about half the size

title: Raccoon scat
def: Raccoon scat is a blunt-ended, tubular dropping often full of seeds and shell bits, left in piles called latrines on logs, rocks, roofs, or at tree bases.
look: dark tubes about 3/4 inch (2 cm) wide with blunt ends
many droppings of different ages in one spot
use: A latrine means raccoons use the site regularly. Keep food and trash locked away.
not: Raccoon latrines can carry roundworm eggs that seriously harm people. Do not touch, sweep, or kick them; keep children and pets away. Clean up only with gloves and a mask and follow CDC guidance.
alike: Coyote scat: twisted with hair and bone, single on trails
Skunk scat: similar but smaller and more often full of insect parts

title: Rabbit or hare scat
def: Rabbit and hare scat is a scatter of round, slightly flattened, pea-sized pellets of chewed plant fiber.
look: round, about 1/4 to 1/2 inch (0.6 to 1.3 cm) across, flattened like a thick coin
light brown and fibrous inside
use: Lots of pellets near brush and browsed twigs mean rabbits or hares feed and hide there.
not: Do not touch or sniff scat with bare hands; use a stick, and wash your hands after. Do not camp next to a latrine or fresh bear sign. Wear gloves when handling rabbits or hares, because of tularemia.
alike: Deer scat: oval or acorn-shaped with a point, larger and darker
Woodchuck or squirrel: smaller, more oblong
ask: Tell me about rabbit or hare scat

title: Bear tracks
def: A black bear track is a wide print with five toes in an arc and a broad pad, the hind print looking like a flat-footed human foot.
look: front print about 4 to 6 inches (10 to 15 cm) wide with claw dots
hind print longer, up to about 7 inches (18 cm), with a heel
use: Fresh tracks mean a bear is close. Make noise, keep food sealed, and keep dogs leashed.
not: Do not follow fresh bear tracks, especially to a carcass or with cubs nearby.
alike: Human barefoot print: big toe on the inside and an arch
Raccoon: much smaller, long fingers

title: Coyote, fox, or dog tracks
def: A canine track has four toes with claw marks around a triangular pad, and an X shape can be drawn through the space between toes and pad.
look: oval print; coyote about 2 1/2 inches (6 cm) long, fox smaller
wild canines walk in a straight, direct line; dogs wander
use: A straight, purposeful line of oval prints is usually a coyote or fox; a zigzagging line beside a person's tracks is usually a dog.
not: Track size alone does not separate a big fox from a small coyote or dog.
alike: Bobcat: round print, no claw marks, three-lobed pad
Raccoon: five long fingers
ask: Tell me about coyote, fox, or dog tracks

title: Raccoon tracks
def: A raccoon track has five long, finger-like toes, like a small human handprint, usually in mud near water.
look: front print about 2 to 3 inches (5 to 8 cm) with separated fingers
hind print longer, like a small foot
use: Raccoon tracks near camp mean you should lock up food at night.
not: Do not handle a raccoon that is active by day and acting oddly; it may have rabies.
alike: Opossum: hind foot has a thumb pointing sideways
Skunk: shorter toes, five in an arc

title: Moose tracks
def: A moose track is a large split-hoof print over 4 inches (10 cm) long, shaped like a deer track but much bigger.
look: blunt or pointed heart shape, about 4 to 6 inches (10 to 15 cm) long
deep in mud or snow, with dewclaws often showing
use: Fresh tracks mean moose are near; give them room, especially in fall and in calving season.
not: Do not follow fresh moose tracks into thick cover.
alike: Deer track: same shape but under about 3 1/2 inches (9 cm)
Cattle: rounder, wider toes

title: Turkey tracks
def: A wild turkey track is a large bird print with three long forward toes and a short back toe, about 4 to 5 inches (10 to 13 cm) long.
look: middle toe longest and straight ahead
long stride of many prints in a line
use: Fresh tracks near fields, roosts, or dusting spots mean turkeys use the area.
not: Tracks do not tell a tom from a hen reliably; large tracks over about 4 1/2 inches are more often toms.
alike: Great blue heron: longer back toe and slimmer toes
Grouse: smaller, about 2 inches (5 cm)

title: Bobcat tracks
def: A bobcat track is a round print about 2 inches (5 cm) across with four toes, no claw marks, and a three-lobed pad.
look: round, not oval like a canine
leading edge of the pad has two notches making three lobes
use: A round print with no claws is a cat; bobcats often walk with hind feet placed in the front prints.
not: Do not track a bobcat closely to a den.
alike: Canine: oval with claw marks and a triangular pad
House cat: smaller, about 1 1/2 inches (4 cm)

title: Rabbit or hare tracks
def: Rabbit and hare tracks come in groups of four: two long hind feet side by side in front of two small front feet, one behind the other.
look: Y-shaped or triangle-shaped track group
snowshoe hare hind prints very large and splayed in snow
use: The big hind prints land ahead of the front prints, so the wide end of the group points the way the animal went.
not: Do not mistake the order: the large prints are in front because the hind feet swing past.
alike: Squirrel: front prints side by side too, with clear toes and claws
ask: Tell me about rabbit or hare tracks
